summary: A humorous local-news write-up of a neighborhood youth talent show called "So You Think You Can Juggle," set for September 12, 2023 at the local theatre. It recounts the quirky acts, from a rabbit vanishing trick to singing Corgis and a kazoo underdog, and the celebrity judges. The piece frames the annual event as a warm, comical community bonding night celebrating kids' imagination.
one_line: Tongue-in-cheek recap of a neighborhood youth talent show, "So You Think You Can Juggle," featuring comical acts and community spirit.
key_facts: The youth talent show "So You Think You Can Juggle" was slated to kick off on the evening of September 12, 2023.
The show is held in the neighborhood theatre and is an annual event.
The lineup was curated by Ms. Betty Leotard, a retired gym teacher and self-proclaimed talent magnet.
Big Joe, owner of the town's only 24-hour diner, sits on the panel of local "celebrity" judges.
On September 11, a warm-up act at the community center featured Simon, reigning champion of the "Most Pogo-stick Jumps in a Minute" award.
The opening act was the Thompson twins, performing an interpretive dance with hula-hoops, ribbon twirling and interpretive charades.

Archie, the "closet conjurer," tried to make his pet rabbit Muffin vanish in a cloud of smoke; a smoke-to-rabbit miscalculation left the audience coughing, and Muffin was found unharmed behind the curtain.
Linda, the neighborhood's dog whisperer, led her pack of 'singing' Corgis using a pitch pipe, producing a "canine cacophony."
The Jones family spun plates while reciting Shakespeare, including "To spin or not to spin."
Timmy Spencer, the dark horse, performed a symphonic suite on a kazoo that was touching and slightly out of tune.
A one-man band juggled instruments while playing them, from a harmonica to a kick drum tied to his back.
Big Joe and the other judges tallied the scores as the performers awaited the result.
